state: Specify native capability contracts for a Can test suite authored by AI agents. Ordinary unrestricted Can functions own scenario order, expected values, scheduling, readiness/retries and reports; authored foreign harnesses must disappear. The chosen execution uses a qualified reference compiler/runtime for the Can controller and fresh Bun case processes, with candidate compilers/runtime/browser artifacts only as subjects and a generic Go supervisor outside them. No implementation, live trials or measurements are authorized; laptop load/storage are bounded. Current assertion supervision kills its direct worker, buffers output before truncating, and does not establish complete filesystem/descendant cleanup. Current process::run uses detached Bun.spawn children and registers cleanup after spawn, but worker SIGKILL skips worker-local cleanup. New resources therefore need reservations and ownership outside the worker before exposure, operation IDs with argument digests, bounded event/byte streams, explicit partial effects and recovery. Absolute path validation alone is not confinement; OS-enforced disk/descendant guarantees must be qualified or refused as unsupported. Native process start/signal returns execution/delivery facts, never server readiness; nonzero exits are observations. A deadline during a state-changing operation can leave an accepted effect with an unknown result, so Can must not blindly retry it. Browser tests require physical and synthetic actions, independent property versus attribute reads, interception with deferred Can decisions, and an armed-before-navigation event stream closed by a bounded drain/seal barrier. Remote Firefox sessions may be owned while the service is shared. JS-source eval or a native whole-scenario helper would retain host-authored policy. Typed native value constructors, one-operation observers and counters can expose proxies/getters/thenables/raw identity; ordinary compiled Can probe programs can handle additional callback logic in the candidate realm. Expected results stay Can-owned and native handles do not cross process heaps. Native fault masking must affect disposable candidate processes, not the trusted judge. SQL facts must come through an independently identified connection/decoder with raw values. Compiler CheckSnapshot performs inert frontend analysis and gives code/severity/UTF16 spans, but folds project failures into diagnostics and omits per-diagnostic phase provenance. A proposed general canlc check --json product CLI needs explicit complete accepted/rejected versus infrastructure-failure statuses, diagnostic stage provenance, versioned schema and source identities. It must not run assertions, emit/publish or execute subjects. Candidate command crashes, malformed reports, cancellation and IO failures cannot count as expected source rejection. This CLI work must classify failures at their source rather than infer them from diagnostic strings.

resource_authority.instructions: Which ownership contract should these shared native operations adopt?

criteria.outside_worker: Reserve and retain resource authority in a native owner outside workers before exposure; use operation IDs, explicit uncertain/partial outcomes, bounded cleanup receipts and host enforcement admission.
criteria.worker_scopes: Keep resource authority in worker-local scopes and ordinary Can teardown, with the outer supervisor only terminating/reaping the worker and reporting abandoned resource risk.
criteria.recovery_scan: Launch resources from workers and rely on later native scanning of process/path ownership records to recover abandoned work, minimizing synchronous broker participation but accepting an acquisition recovery window.

observation_boundary.instructions: Which boundary should define browser and independent native observations?

criteria.typed_facts: Expose bounded typed actions, event streams, foreign-value construction and individual facts; Can chooses order and expectations, with ordinary Can probes for richer callbacks and no foreign-source escape hatch.
criteria.source_eval: Allow Can to submit JavaScript source to browser/native contexts and compare returned data in Can, retaining foreign-authored callbacks as part of the testing contract.
criteria.scenario_adapters: Provide native operations for entire browser/native scenario families returning result summaries, with Can handling registration and final comparisons.

compiler_diagnostics.instructions: Which compiler-diagnostic boundary should this contract choose?

criteria.product_cli: Define general canlc check --json with explicit frontend fault/phase provenance and complete-report statuses; use generic managed-process execution and Can report parsing/expectations.
criteria.language_primitive: Expose semantic compiler checking as a new native Can operation with explicit candidate identity and isolation, designing its binding/protocol instead of a public CLI first.
criteria.stderr_adapter: Keep existing compiler commands and define a Can stderr/status parser as the primary rejection interface, maintaining wording/phase parsing without a new structured product command.
